_purpose: Controlled vocabularies the health auditor validates against, so a typo or a fabricated identifier is caught before it corrupts a query. Deterministic allow-lists only — never fabricate an entry to make a check pass; add the real canonical name.

framework_names._note: Canonical framework names as they must appear in crosswalk/catalog data. A name not on this list (e.g. 'ISO 27001' missing the '/IEC') is flagged so overlap queries don't silently miss it.

framework_aliases._note: Canonical framework labels for the master mapping surface (Phase 19) and the aliases each surface uses for the SAME framework+version. Resolution rule: explicit alias wins; any label with no alias row resolves to ITSELF (identity) — version-ambiguous labels (e.g. bare 'ISO/IEC 27001', hub-era 'NIST CSF') deliberately stay distinct canonicals rather than fabricating a version equivalence. Loaded into grc.db as framework_labels.

SOC 2.note: Native ids are AICPA TSC criteria (CC/A/C/PI/P) — SOC 2 has no universal control list; firm-local ids never appear.

SOC 1.note: No public control layer (SSAE 22 / AT-C 320) — master surface exposes SOC 1 as a data gap; overlap via inferred_er only.

SCF 2026.1.note: Owner meta-framework; scf_direct projection edges are SCF/CAP-scope acceptance rules (acceptance-authority model).

CSA CCM v4.note: ccm_oscal projection edges are CSA-STAR-scope acceptance rules (source-stated equivalent-to/superset-of from the v4.0.12 OSCAL mapping-collection).

deliberately_distinct._note: Labels that LOOK like aliases but are different frameworks or unpinned versions — resolved to themselves, never merged.

ambiguous._note: Shorthand that maps to more than one framework family. Resolvers raise rather than guess (framework_alias.AmbiguousFrameworkError) — a wrong framework answer is worse than no answer. Phase 35: 'csf' silently returned HITRUST CSF on the master surface because that label sorts first alphabetically.

csf.reason: CSF is the common shorthand for both the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the HITRUST CSF

data_gaps._note: Framework/surface pairs with no rows BY FACT, not by defect. A resolver may return nothing here without it being a bug; test_alias_contract asserts each declaration still matches the data.

soc 1.reason: SSAE 22 / AT-C 320 defines report standards, not a public control catalog — the master surface exposes SOC 1 as a data gap (dbz_query._master_soc1_gap)

soc1.reason: SSAE 22 / AT-C 320 defines report standards, not a public control catalog — the master surface exposes SOC 1 as a data gap (dbz_query._master_soc1_gap)

fedramp.reason: FedRAMP r5 is a baseline overlay on the 800-53 spine, not a separate mapped framework: it carries projection rows (overlap) but no master or unified edges

fedramp r5.reason: FedRAMP r5 is a baseline overlay on the 800-53 spine, not a separate mapped framework: it carries projection rows (overlap) but no master or unified edges

hipaa.reason: the unified (legacy) surface carries only HIPAA Privacy Rule rows; HIPAA Security lives on the spine/master surfaces. Resolving 'hipaa' to the Privacy Rule there would answer a different rule than the user asked for

nist 800-172.reason: the 2021 edition is dual-pinned for CMMC Level 3 reference only; the mapped artifact is NIST SP 800-172 r3

800-53.reason: the unified (legacy) surface carries only the Rev 4 Appendix J privacy catalog under an 800-53 name; the r5 spine is the master/projection surfaces

nist sp 800-53.reason: the unified (legacy) surface carries only the Rev 4 Appendix J privacy catalog under an 800-53 name; the r5 spine is the master/projection surfaces

family_groups._note: Shorthand whose program reality spans MORE THAN ONE canonical label because an external authority makes them one thing. Only added with the instrument cited — never as a convenience, and never to merge versions (that is what deliberately_distinct forbids). Resolvers fan a group out across whichever members the queried surface carries; rows keep their true labels.

cmmc.basis: CMMC Level 2 assesses against NIST SP 800-171 r2 (DoD class deviation, May 2024; reaffirmed by the July-2026 Phase 2 suspension memo). Revisit when the assessment basis moves to r3.

relationship_types._note: Mirrors VALID_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES in cross-mapping/nist-catalog/ingestion/validate_catalog.py — kept in sync so the auditor and the catalog validator agree.

regulatory_provenance._purpose: Controlled vocabulary for horizon/changelog provenance blocks (protocol-layer/regulatory-provenance.md).

edge_semantics._note: What a master edge CLAIMS — orthogonal to confidence, which says how SURE we are. Phase 36 (finding F-10) found the repo stored a source's weak 'relates to' link in the same shape as a strong 'satisfies' link, and the overlap engine then reported the result as shared audit work. This vocabulary makes strength explicit. Classes are DERIVED MECHANICALLY from relationship_basis + relationship — no per-edge judgment is applied and no new data is invented; validate_spine asserts the derivation is total and single-valued. NOTE (phase 37): authority is read from the TIER, not from relationship_basis. NIST's own OLIR exports carry relationship_basis=derived_cardinality because the export supplies no relationship TYPE — but NIST published the mapping, so those edges are source-stated and must not be demoted to 'informs'.

equivalent.definition: A source states the two requirements are the same requirement.
equivalent.derived_from: tier in (owner_direct, nist_stated, owner_stated) AND relationship=equal — the source published the mapping AND states the two are the same requirement

supports.definition: A source states a directional or partial satisfaction relationship (subset/superset/intersect), or several independent sources agree the pair is related.
supports.derived_from: tier in (owner_direct, nist_stated, owner_stated) — the source published the mapping (a stated relationship type may or may not accompany it); or relationship_basis=multi_source_consensus (several independent sources agree)

co_referenced.definition: One hub requirement (or one production evidence request) cited both sides. Topical co-occurrence, NOT a stated claim that doing one contributes to the other.

informs.definition: Structural or bibliographic association only — co-citation in a compiled crosswalk, or a relationship inferred from cardinality rather than stated.
informs.derived_from: everything else — a compiled/bundled crosswalk (co_citation) or a relationship inferred from cardinality with no publishing authority behind it

cci_confirmation._note: Verdict on a framework->CCI mapping: is it WITNESSED or merely reachable? The point of this repository is convergence onto confirmed CCI mappings; before phase 38 frameworks reached CCIs only by transitive join (framework -> r5 sub-part -> cci_bridge), which asserts a path exists, never that anyone checked it. Witnesses are independent by construction and the verdict is derived mechanically (cci_confirm.py); validate_spine asserts totality. 'reachable' must never be presented as a mapping.

confirmed.definition: The CCI's own 800-53 anchor is multi-witness confirmed AND at least two independent agreement witnesses exist, at least one of them CCI-level (a second publisher on this anchor, or a STIG rule exercising this CCI).

corroborated.definition: The CCI anchor is confirmed and exactly one agreement witness exists.

reachable.definition: The transitive join holds and the CCI anchor is confirmed, but nothing independently corroborates the framework's claim. NOT a mapping — this is the state everything was in before phase 38.

weak.definition: The CCI's own 800-53 anchor is disa_only or candidate, so nothing above it can be confirmed.

witnesses.w_framework_sources: distinct mapping publishers placing this control on this anchor (framework_projection.provenance); CCI-level
witnesses.w_cci_anchor_confirmed: cci_mapping_corroboration.verdict='confirmed' — the CCI->800-53 link is itself multi-witness; prerequisite
witnesses.w_stig_exercised: a real STIG rule exercises this CCI (stig_cci_usage); CCI-level
witnesses.w_consensus: another framework independently agrees on this control (consensus_edges strong/moderate). Matched at CONTROL granularity, so it supports but never alone carries a confirmation
witnesses.w_subpart_precision: anchored at sub-part rather than whole control — a precision signal, never an agreement witness
